title: One On One · Daryl Hall & John Oates · 1982
dek: Side two of H2O. Daryl Hall lead, Charlie DeChant on tenor, the saxophone doing as much of the talking as the voice.
body:
H2O came out in October 1982 and most of the room remembers it for *Maneater*. *One On One* is the other thing that record did — slower, warmer, the sports metaphor sitting on top of a quiet R&B groove.

Hall wrote it as a love song dressed in a basketball court. *I'm tired of playing on the team / It seems I don't get time out anymore.* The trick is that the metaphor never gets cute — the song just lets the saxophone answer back every time the voice asks the question.

A Tuesday-evening song. Coffee pot still on, the room a little dimmer than it was an hour ago.
